topics: Introduction to Computational Geometry:-  Basics of Computational Geometry  - Introduction and applications of computational geometry
Basic geometric primitives: points, lines, segments, polygons (Text 1, Chapters 1, 2)
Convex Hulls  - Definition and properties of convex hulls
Divide and conquer algorithm for convex hulls (Text 2, Section 33.3)
Line Segment Intersection  - Problem definition and applications
Range Searching  - Problem definition and applications
Point Location  - Problem definition and applications
Trapezoidal map and randomized incremental algorithm
Binary Space Partitioning  - Definition and applications
Use in computer graphics and collision detection (Text 1, Chapter 12)
Arrangements of Lines and Duality  - Arrangements of lines and complexity
Duality transform and its applications (Text 1, Chapter 8)
Motion Planning and Geometric Optimization  - Problem definition and applications
Visibility graphs and shortest path problems
Computational Geometry in Practice  - Computational geometry libraries and software
Applications in robotics, computer graphics, GIS (Text 3, Chapters 9, 10)

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks.  Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.  Each question can have a maximum of 3 subdivisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Understand Fundamental Concepts and Applications of Computational Geometry
Apply Algorithms for Convex Hulls and Line Segment Intersection Algorithms
Perform Polygon Triangulation and Understand Voronoi Diagrams
Build Delaunay Triangulations and Range Searching Techniques
Apply Advanced Computational Geometry Techniques and Algorithms
